- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/841
- **Title**: gh-840 [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-840` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1084
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T13:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:17:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The fail-closed design (pure module, machine-gated markers, forge-resistant parsing, comprehensive RED→GREEN tests, hoisted require per gh-823) is solid and both suites pass locally (16/16 unit, 481/481 smAgent). However, the whole mechanism reads the PR head from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which the query layer leaves `null` for both affected rules — so in production no consumption marker is ever stamped and the sweep's latch/in-flight/head-advanced gates are dead code (see blocking comment). One important design gap: any head move (including a silent branch refresh) counts as a "rework close", letting the exact hang this PR fixes slip past the sweep.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `js/smAgent.js:4119` — head sourced from `ticket.pr.headSha` is always `null` for PR-carrier rules (`queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`); audit markers are silently never posted, the sweep never has evidence, and its head-dependent gates no-op. Fix via the existing `prHeadAndLabels` probe + a live-shape (`pr: null`) test.
- ⚠️ `js/smAgent.js:4203` — `headAdvanced` treats any head move as a close proof; a silent refresh after a bogus consumption suppresses the sweep forever with machine threads still open.
- 💡 `js/smAgent.js:4096` — `pullRequestId: prNumber` not stringified (siblings all use `String(prNumber)`).

**Next Steps**:
1. Probe the head via `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` (fallback) in `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`; warn when a consumption can't be attributed.
2. Add tests with the live item shape (`pr: null`) — current fixtures inject `pr.headSha`, masking the defect.
3. Corroborate `head-advanced` (e.g. a concluded leg run on the current head) or restore when machine threads remain open on the advanced head.
4. Follow-up ticket: `arm_rework` (rework-unresolved-threads) shares the same null-`item.pr` assumption, so the gh-806 latch is inert on the PR-carrier arming path too.

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...
headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,
```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

**Suggestion:** only accept `head-advanced` as close proof when corroborated — e.g. require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp (`headWorkflowRunsSafe` is already fetched two lines above for the in-flight check, so this is cheap), or fall through to restore when unresolved *machine* threads still exist on the advanced head (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is evidence of a refresh, not a close). If the deliberate tradeoff is kept, it should be documented in the rule description in `sm_github.json` so the next incident review doesn't misread `'head-advanced'` skips as healthy closes.

+/**
+ * reworkConsumption.js — fail-closed `agent:rework` consumption bookkeeping
+ * and the consumed-without-work sweep decision (gh-840).
+ *
+ * Live pathology (dmtools-agents PR #826 / gh-825, 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z):
+ * `agent:rework` was armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED —
+ * yet no rework leg ever ran, no fix commit landed on the head, 4/6 review
+ * threads stayed unresolved and no closing bookkeeping comment existed.
+ * Root cause: the PR-carrier rule's `consumeLabels` removes the label on
+ * dispatch (or on the gh-715 cross-anchor suppression — any leg in flight
+ * under the other anchor "fulfills" the request, even a REVIEW leg), with
+ * nothing recording the consumption and nothing verifying a leg-close
+ * marker. The armer that should have recovered (arm_rework /
+ * rework-unresolved-threads) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch,
+ * gh-807 verdict gate, agent:review notLabels), so the arm never returned:
+ * 4h+ hang.
+ *
+ * This module is the pure side of the fix:
+ *
+ *   Audit log  — every consumption posts ONE machine-parseable marker
+ *                comment on the PR recording its path (dispatch |
+ *                cross-anchor), the head sha and a timestamp. Markers are
+ *                trusted only from machine identities (the same allowlist
+ *                doctrine as reviewVerdicts.js — the format is public).
+ *   Sweep      — shouldRestoreArm(): a PR with unresolved MACHINE review
+ *                threads, no agent:rework label, no rework in flight,
+ *                evidence of a prior consumption (consume/restore marker),
+ *                quiet longer than staleMs (default 30 min ≈ 6 ticks at a
+ *                ~5-min cron) → restore the arm. Fail-closed everywhere:
+ *                no evidence, no restore (AC3 — human-thread-only PRs are
+ *                untouched); no clock, no restore. The close proof is
+ *                thread OWNERSHIP, not head position (gh-840 rework
+ *                review, IMPORTANT): a head move with the same open
+ *                machine threads is a silentUpdateBranch refresh, not a
+ *                close — a healthy close resolves the machine threads
+ *                ('no-unresolved-threads'); a bare head advance must never
+ *                suppress the sweep.
+ *
+ * Pure module — no dmtools globals; smAgent feeds it comment payloads and
+ * applies the decisions. GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, JSON-safe
+ * data only).
+ */
+'use strict';
+
+// gh-840 AC1 bound: N ticks. The SM cron ticks every ~5 min; 30 min = 6
+// ticks — the ticket's "≤6 ticks" self-heal bound. Deployment-tunable via
+// the rule's staleMinutes knob (same shape as sweep_stale_validation).
+var DEFAULT_RESTORE_STALE_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;
+
+// The consumption audit marker — one line, JSON payload, invisible in the
+// rendered PR (same protocol family as the gh-807 verdict marker).
+var CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-consume ';
+var RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-restore ';
+var MARKER_SUFFIX = ' -->';
+
+// The only legal consumption paths (the guard vocabulary):
+//   'dispatch'      — consumeLabels fired after an accepted workflow_dispatch
+//   'cross-anchor'  — consumeLabels fired after the gh-715 cross-anchor
+//                     suppression consumed the request
+var CONSUME_PATHS = ['dispatch', 'cross-anchor'];
+
+function isLegalConsumePath(path) {
+    return CONSUME_PATHS.indexOf(path) !== -1;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the consumption-audit comment body. path must be one of
+ * CONSUME_PATHS; headSha anchors the consumption to the head it was
+ * supposed to rework (the sweep's close-proof check compares the recorded
+ * head against the live head). Returns null on an unbuildable record —
+ * callers skip the post; an unattributed consumption must never exist.
+ */
+function buildConsumeAuditComment(path, headSha, atIso) {
+    if (!isLegalConsumePath(path)) return null;
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        path: path,
+        head: headSha,
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🏷️ agent:rework consumed (path: ' + path + ', head ' +
+        String(headSha).substring(0, 7) + ') — gh-840 consumption audit. ' +
+        'The label must come off ONLY via a successful rework close; if no close ' +
+        'follows, the tick sweep re-arms it.';
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the sweep's restore bookkeeping marker (gh-821-style durability:
+ * the next ticks read it as the newest quiet-window anchor, so a restore
+ * whose arm is re-consumed without work re-enters the same bounded cycle
+ * instead of being mistaken for fresh state).
+ */
+function buildRestoreMarkerComment(headSha, reason, atIso) {
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        head: headSha,
+        reason: reason || 'restore',
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🔄 rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved (gh-840).';
+}
+
+function extractMarker(body, prefix) {
+    var text = String(body || '');
+    var start = text.indexOf(prefix);
+    if (start === -1) return null;
+    start += prefix.length;
+    var end = text.indexOf(MARKER_SUFFIX, start);
+    if (end === -1) return null;
+    var raw = text.substring(start, end).trim();
+    var parsed;
+    try { parsed = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return null; }

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). 1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

If the deliberate tradeoff is kept, it should be documented in the rule description in `sm_github.json` so the next incident review doesn't misread `'head-advanced'` skips as healthy closes.

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause

- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...
headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,
```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

**Suggestion:** only accept `head-advanced` as close proof when corroborated — e.g. require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp (`headWorkflowRunsSafe` is already fetched two lines above for the in-flight check, so this is cheap), or fall through to restore when unresolved *machine* threads still exist on the advanced head (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is evidence of a refresh, not a close). If the deliberate tradeoff is kept, it should be documented in the rule description in `sm_github.json` so the next incident review doesn't misread `'head-advanced'` skips as healthy closes.

+/**
+ * reworkConsumption.js — fail-closed `agent:rework` consumption bookkeeping
+ * and the consumed-without-work sweep decision (gh-840).
+ *
+ * Live pathology (dmtools-agents PR #826 / gh-825, 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z):
+ * `agent:rework` was armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED —
+ * yet no rework leg ever ran, no fix commit landed on the head, 4/6 review
+ * threads stayed unresolved and no closing bookkeeping comment existed.
+ * Root cause: the PR-carrier rule's `consumeLabels` removes the label on
+ * dispatch (or on the gh-715 cross-anchor suppression — any leg in flight
+ * under the other anchor "fulfills" the request, even a REVIEW leg), with
+ * nothing recording the consumption and nothing verifying a leg-close
+ * marker. The armer that should have recovered (arm_rework /
+ * rework-unresolved-threads) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch,
+ * gh-807 verdict gate, agent:review notLabels), so the arm never returned:
+ * 4h+ hang.
+ *
+ * This module is the pure side of the fix:
+ *
+ *   Audit log  — every consumption posts ONE machine-parseable marker
+ *                comment on the PR recording its path (dispatch |
+ *                cross-anchor), the head sha and a timestamp. Markers are
+ *                trusted only from machine identities (the same allowlist
+ *                doctrine as reviewVerdicts.js — the format is public).
+ *   Sweep      — shouldRestoreArm(): a PR with unresolved MACHINE review
+ *                threads, no agent:rework label, no rework in flight,
+ *                evidence of a prior consumption (consume/restore marker),
+ *                quiet longer than staleMs (default 30 min ≈ 6 ticks at a
+ *                ~5-min cron) → restore the arm. Fail-closed everywhere:
+ *                no evidence, no restore (AC3 — human-thread-only PRs are
+ *                untouched); no clock, no restore. The close proof is
+ *                thread OWNERSHIP, not head position (gh-840 rework
+ *                review, IMPORTANT): a head move with the same open
+ *                machine threads is a silentUpdateBranch refresh, not a
+ *                close — a healthy close resolves the machine threads
+ *                ('no-unresolved-threads'); a bare head advance must never
+ *                suppress the sweep.
+ *
+ * Pure module — no dmtools globals; smAgent feeds it comment payloads and
+ * applies the decisions. GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, JSON-safe
+ * data only).
+ */
+'use strict';
+
+// gh-840 AC1 bound: N ticks. The SM cron ticks every ~5 min; 30 min = 6
+// ticks — the ticket's "≤6 ticks" self-heal bound. Deployment-tunable via
+// the rule's staleMinutes knob (same shape as sweep_stale_validation).
+var DEFAULT_RESTORE_STALE_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;
+
+// The consumption audit marker — one line, JSON payload, invisible in the
+// rendered PR (same protocol family as the gh-807 verdict marker).
+var CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-consume ';
+var RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-restore ';
+var MARKER_SUFFIX = ' -->';
+
+// The only legal consumption paths (the guard vocabulary):
+//   'dispatch'      — consumeLabels fired after an accepted workflow_dispatch
+//   'cross-anchor'  — consumeLabels fired after the gh-715 cross-anchor
+//                     suppression consumed the request
+var CONSUME_PATHS = ['dispatch', 'cross-anchor'];
+
+function isLegalConsumePath(path) {
+    return CONSUME_PATHS.indexOf(path) !== -1;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the consumption-audit comment body. path must be one of
+ * CONSUME_PATHS; headSha anchors the consumption to the head it was
+ * supposed to rework (the sweep's close-proof check compares the recorded
+ * head against the live head). Returns null on an unbuildable record —
+ * callers skip the post; an unattributed consumption must never exist.
+ */
+function buildConsumeAuditComment(path, headSha, atIso) {
+    if (!isLegalConsumePath(path)) return null;
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        path: path,
+        head: headSha,
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🏷️ agent:rework consumed (path: ' + path + ', head ' +
+        String(headSha).substring(0, 7) + ') — gh-840 consumption audit. ' +
+        'The label must come off ONLY via a successful rework close; if no close ' +
+        'follows, the tick sweep re-arms it.';
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the sweep's restore bookkeeping marker (gh-821-style durability:
+ * the next ticks read it as the newest quiet-window anchor, so a restore
+ * whose arm is re-consumed without work re-enters the same bounded cycle
+ * instead of being mistaken for fresh state).
+ */
+function buildRestoreMarkerComment(headSha, reason, atIso) {
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        head: headSha,
+        reason: reason || 'restore',
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🔄 rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved (gh-840).';
+}
+
+function extractMarker(body, prefix) {
+    var text = String(body || '');
+    var start = text.indexOf(prefix);
+    if (start === -1) return null;
+    start += prefix.length;
+    var end = text.indexOf(MARKER_SUFFIX, start);
+    if (end === -1) return null;
+    var raw = text.substring(start, end).trim();
+    var parsed;
+    try { parsed = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return null; }

+ *                doctrine as reviewVerdicts.js — the format is public).
+ *   Sweep      — shouldRestoreArm(): a PR with unresolved MACHINE review
+ *                threads, no agent:rework label, no rework in flight,
+ *                evidence of a prior consumption (consume/restore marker),
+ *                quiet longer than staleMs (default 30 min ≈ 6 ticks at a
+ *                ~5-min cron) → restore the arm. Fail-closed everywhere:
+ *                no evidence, no restore (AC3 — human-thread-only PRs are
+ *                untouched); no clock, no restore. The close proof is
+ *                thread OWNERSHIP, not head position (gh-840 rework
+ *                review, IMPORTANT): a head move with the same open
+ *                machine threads is a silentUpdateBranch refresh, not a
+ *                close — a healthy close resolves the machine threads
+ *                ('no-unresolved-threads'); a bare head advance must never
+ *                suppress the sweep.
+ *
+ * Pure module — no dmtools globals; smAgent feeds it comment payloads and
+ * applies the decisions. GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, JSON-safe
+ * data only).
+ */
+'use strict';
+
+// gh-840 AC1 bound: N ticks. The SM cron ticks every ~5 min; 30 min = 6
+// ticks — the ticket's "≤6 ticks" self-heal bound. Deployment-tunable via
+// the rule's staleMinutes knob (same shape as sweep_stale_validation).
+var DEFAULT_RESTORE_STALE_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;
+
+// The consumption audit marker — one line, JSON payload, invisible in the
+// rendered PR (same protocol family as the gh-807 verdict marker).
+var CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-consume ';
+var RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-restore ';
+var MARKER_SUFFIX = ' -->';
+
+// The only legal consumption paths (the guard vocabulary):
+//   'dispatch'      — consumeLabels fired after an accepted workflow_dispatch
+//   'cross-anchor'  — consumeLabels fired after the gh-715 cross-anchor
+//                     suppression consumed the request
+var CONSUME_PATHS = ['dispatch', 'cross-anchor'];
+
+function isLegalConsumePath(path) {
+    return CONSUME_PATHS.indexOf(path) !== -1;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the consumption-audit comment body. path must be one of
+ * CONSUME_PATHS; headSha anchors the consumption to the head it was
+ * supposed to rework (the sweep's close-proof check compares the recorded
+ * head against the live head). Returns null on an unbuildable record —
+ * callers skip the post; an unattributed consumption must never exist.
+ */
+function buildConsumeAuditComment(path, headSha, atIso) {
+    if (!isLegalConsumePath(path)) return null;
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        path: path,
+        head: headSha,
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🏷️ agent:rework consumed (path: ' + path + ', head ' +
+        String(headSha).substring(0, 7) + ') — gh-840 consumption audit. ' +
+        'The label must come off ONLY via a successful rework close; if no close ' +
+        'follows, the tick sweep re-arms it.';
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the sweep's restore bookkeeping marker (gh-821-style durability:
+ * the next ticks read it as the newest quiet-window anchor, so a restore
+ * whose arm is re-consumed without work re-enters the same bounded cycle
+ * instead of being mistaken for fresh state).
+ */
+function buildRestoreMarkerComment(headSha, reason, atIso) {
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        head: headSha,
+        reason: reason || 'restore',
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🔄 rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved (gh-840).';
+}
+
+function extractMarker(body, prefix) {
+    var text = String(body || '');
+    var start = text.indexOf(prefix);
+    if (start === -1) return null;
+    start += prefix.length;
+    var end = text.indexOf(MARKER_SUFFIX, start);
+    if (end === -1) return null;
+    var raw = text.substring(start, end).trim();
+    var parsed;
+    try { parsed = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return null; }

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...
headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,
```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

**Suggestion:** only accept `head-advanced` as close proof when corroborated — e.g. require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp (`headWorkflowRunsSafe` is already fetched two lines above for the in-flight check, so this is cheap), or fall through to restore when unresolved *machine* threads still exist on the advanced head (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is evidence of a refresh, not a close). If the deliberate tradeoff is kept, it should be documented in the rule description in `sm_github.json` so the next incident review doesn't misread `'head-advanced'` skips as healthy closes.

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

+/**
+ * reworkConsumption.js — fail-closed `agent:rework` consumption bookkeeping
+ * and the consumed-without-work sweep decision (gh-840).
+ *
+ * Live pathology (dmtools-agents PR #826 / gh-825, 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z):
+ * `agent:rework` was armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED —
+ * yet no rework leg ever ran, no fix commit landed on the head, 4/6 review
+ * threads stayed unresolved and no closing bookkeeping comment existed.
+ * Root cause: the PR-carrier rule's `consumeLabels` removes the label on
+ * dispatch (or on the gh-715 cross-anchor suppression — any leg in flight
+ * under the other anchor "fulfills" the request, even a REVIEW leg), with
+ * nothing recording the consumption and nothing verifying a leg-close
+ * marker. The armer that should have recovered (arm_rework /
+ * rework-unresolved-threads) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch,
+ * gh-807 verdict gate, agent:review notLabels), so the arm never returned:
+ * 4h+ hang.
+ *
+ * This module is the pure side of the fix:
+ *
+ *   Audit log  — every consumption posts ONE machine-parseable marker
+ *                comment on the PR recording its path (dispatch |
+ *                cross-anchor), the head sha and a timestamp. Markers are
+ *                trusted only from machine identities (the same allowlist
+ *                doctrine as reviewVerdicts.js — the format is public).
+ *   Sweep      — shouldRestoreArm(): a PR with unresolved MACHINE review
+ *                threads, no agent:rework label, no rework in flight,
+ *                evidence of a prior consumption (consume/restore marker),
+ *                quiet longer than staleMs (default 30 min ≈ 6 ticks at a
+ *                ~5-min cron) → restore the arm. Fail-closed everywhere:
+ *                no evidence, no restore (AC3 — human-thread-only PRs are
+ *                untouched); no clock, no restore. The close proof is
+ *                thread OWNERSHIP, not head position (gh-840 rework
+ *                review, IMPORTANT): a head move with the same open
+ *                machine threads is a silentUpdateBranch refresh, not a
+ *                close — a healthy close resolves the machine threads
+ *                ('no-unresolved-threads'); a bare head advance must never
+ *                suppress the sweep.
+ *
+ * Pure module — no dmtools globals; smAgent feeds it comment payloads and
+ * applies the decisions. GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, JSON-safe
+ * data only).
+ */
+'use strict';
+
+// gh-840 AC1 bound: N ticks. The SM cron ticks every ~5 min; 30 min = 6
+// ticks — the ticket's "≤6 ticks" self-heal bound. Deployment-tunable via
+// the rule's staleMinutes knob (same shape as sweep_stale_validation).
+var DEFAULT_RESTORE_STALE_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;
+
+// The consumption audit marker — one line, JSON payload, invisible in the
+// rendered PR (same protocol family as the gh-807 verdict marker).
+var CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-consume ';
+var RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-restore ';
+var MARKER_SUFFIX = ' -->';
+
+// The only legal consumption paths (the guard vocabulary):
+//   'dispatch'      — consumeLabels fired after an accepted workflow_dispatch
+//   'cross-anchor'  — consumeLabels fired after the gh-715 cross-anchor
+//                     suppression consumed the request
+var CONSUME_PATHS = ['dispatch', 'cross-anchor'];
+
+function isLegalConsumePath(path) {
+    return CONSUME_PATHS.indexOf(path) !== -1;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the consumption-audit comment body. path must be one of
+ * CONSUME_PATHS; headSha anchors the consumption to the head it was
+ * supposed to rework (the sweep's close-proof check compares the recorded
+ * head against the live head). Returns null on an unbuildable record —
+ * callers skip the post; an unattributed consumption must never exist.
+ */
+function buildConsumeAuditComment(path, headSha, atIso) {
+    if (!isLegalConsumePath(path)) return null;
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        path: path,
+        head: headSha,
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🏷️ agent:rework consumed (path: ' + path + ', head ' +
+        String(headSha).substring(0, 7) + ') — gh-840 consumption audit. ' +
+        'The label must come off ONLY via a successful rework close; if no close ' +
+        'follows, the tick sweep re-arms it.';
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the sweep's restore bookkeeping marker (gh-821-style durability:
+ * the next ticks read it as the newest quiet-window anchor, so a restore
+ * whose arm is re-consumed without work re-enters the same bounded cycle
+ * instead of being mistaken for fresh state).
+ */
+function buildRestoreMarkerComment(headSha, reason, atIso) {
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        head: headSha,
+        reason: reason || 'restore',
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🔄 rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved (gh-840).';
+}
+
+function extractMarker(body, prefix) {
+    var text = String(body || '');
+    var start = text.indexOf(prefix);
+    if (start === -1) return null;
+    start += prefix.length;
+    var end = text.indexOf(MARKER_SUFFIX, start);
+    if (end === -1) return null;
+    var raw = text.substring(start, end).trim();
+    var parsed;
+    try { parsed = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return null; }

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...
headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,
```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

**Suggestion:** only accept `head-advanced` as close proof when corroborated — e.g. require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp (`headWorkflowRunsSafe` is already fetched two lines above for the in-flight check, so this is cheap), or fall through to restore when unresolved *machine* threads still exist on the advanced head (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is evidence of a refresh, not a close). --- /dev/null
+++ b/js/common/reworkConsumption.js
@@ -0,0 +1,240 @@
+/**
+ * reworkConsumption.js — fail-closed `agent:rework` consumption bookkeeping
+ * and the consumed-without-work sweep decision (gh-840).
+ *
+ * Live pathology (dmtools-agents PR #826 / gh-825, 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z):
+ * `agent:rework` was armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED —
+ * yet no rework leg ever ran, no fix commit landed on the head, 4/6 review
+ * threads stayed unresolved and no closing bookkeeping comment existed.
+ * Root cause: the PR-carrier rule's `consumeLabels` removes the label on
+ * dispatch (or on the gh-715 cross-anchor suppression — any leg in flight
+ * under the other anchor "fulfills" the request, even a REVIEW leg), with
+ * nothing recording the consumption and nothing verifying a leg-close
+ * marker. The armer that should have recovered (arm_rework /
+ * rework-unresolved-threads) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch,
+ * gh-807 verdict gate, agent:review notLabels), so the arm never returned:
+ * 4h+ hang.
+ *
+ * This module is the pure side of the fix:
+ *
+ *   Audit log  — every consumption posts ONE machine-parseable marker
+ *                comment on the PR recording its path (dispatch |
+ *                cross-anchor), the head sha and a timestamp. Markers are
+ *                trusted only from machine identities (the same allowlist
+ *                doctrine as reviewVerdicts.js — the format is public).
+ *   Sweep      — shouldRestoreArm(): a PR with unresolved MACHINE review
+ *                threads, no agent:rework label, no rework in flight,
+ *                evidence of a prior consumption (consume/restore marker),
+ *                quiet longer than staleMs (default 30 min ≈ 6 ticks at a
+ *                ~5-min cron) → restore the arm. Fail-closed everywhere:
+ *                no evidence, no restore (AC3 — human-thread-only PRs are
+ *                untouched); no clock, no restore. The close proof is
+ *                thread OWNERSHIP, not head position (gh-840 rework
+ *                review, IMPORTANT): a head move with the same open
+ *                machine threads is a silentUpdateBranch refresh, not a
+ *                close — a healthy close resolves the machine threads
+ *                ('no-unresolved-threads'); a bare head advance must never
+ *                suppress the sweep.
+ *
+ * Pure module — no dmtools globals; smAgent feeds it comment payloads and
+ * applies the decisions. GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, JSON-safe
+ * data only).
+ */
+'use strict';
+
+// gh-840 AC1 bound: N ticks. The SM cron ticks every ~5 min; 30 min = 6
+// ticks — the ticket's "≤6 ticks" self-heal bound. Deployment-tunable via
+// the rule's staleMinutes knob (same shape as sweep_stale_validation).
+var DEFAULT_RESTORE_STALE_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;
+
+// The consumption audit marker — one line, JSON payload, invisible in the
+// rendered PR (same protocol family as the gh-807 verdict marker).
+var CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-consume ';
+var RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-restore ';
+var MARKER_SUFFIX = ' -->';
+
+// The only legal consumption paths (the guard vocabulary):
+//   'dispatch'      — consumeLabels fired after an accepted workflow_dispatch
+//   'cross-anchor'  — consumeLabels fired after the gh-715 cross-anchor
+//                     suppression consumed the request
+var CONSUME_PATHS = ['dispatch', 'cross-anchor'];
+
+function isLegalConsumePath(path) {
+    return CONSUME_PATHS.indexOf(path) !== -1;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the consumption-audit comment body. path must be one of
+ * CONSUME_PATHS; headSha anchors the consumption to the head it was
+ * supposed to rework (the sweep's close-proof check compares the recorded
+ * head against the live head). Returns null on an unbuildable record —
+ * callers skip the post; an unattributed consumption must never exist.
+ */
+function buildConsumeAuditComment(path, headSha, atIso) {
+    if (!isLegalConsumePath(path)) return null;
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        path: path,
+        head: headSha,
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🏷️ agent:rework consumed (path: ' + path + ', head ' +
+        String(headSha).substring(0, 7) + ') — gh-840 consumption audit. ' +
+        'The label must come off ONLY via a successful rework close; if no close ' +
+        'follows, the tick sweep re-arms it.';
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the sweep's restore bookkeeping marker (gh-821-style durability:
+ * the next ticks read it as the newest quiet-window anchor, so a restore
+ * whose arm is re-consumed without work re-enters the same bounded cycle

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

+/**
+ * reworkConsumption.js — fail-closed `agent:rework` consumption bookkeeping
+ * and the consumed-without-work sweep decision (gh-840).
+ *
+ * Live pathology (dmtools-agents PR #826 / gh-825, 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z):
+ * `agent:rework` was armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED —
+ * yet no rework leg ever ran, no fix commit landed on the head, 4/6 review
+ * threads stayed unresolved and no closing bookkeeping comment existed.
+ * Root cause: the PR-carrier rule's `consumeLabels` removes the label on
+ * dispatch (or on the gh-715 cross-anchor suppression — any leg in flight
+ * under the other anchor "fulfills" the request, even a REVIEW leg), with
+ * nothing recording the consumption and nothing verifying a leg-close
+ * marker. The armer that should have recovered (arm_rework /
+ * rework-unresolved-threads) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch,
+ * gh-807 verdict gate, agent:review notLabels), so the arm never returned:
+ * 4h+ hang.
+ *
+ * This module is the pure side of the fix:
+ *
+ *   Audit log  — every consumption posts ONE machine-parseable marker
+ *                comment on the PR recording its path (dispatch |
+ *                cross-anchor), the head sha and a timestamp. Markers are
+ *                trusted only from machine identities (the same allowlist
+ *                doctrine as reviewVerdicts.js — the format is public).
+ *   Sweep      — shouldRestoreArm(): a PR with unresolved MACHINE review
+ *                threads, no agent:rework label, no rework in flight,
+ *                evidence of a prior consumption (consume/restore marker),
+ *                quiet longer than staleMs (default 30 min ≈ 6 ticks at a
+ *                ~5-min cron) → restore the arm. Fail-closed everywhere:
+ *                no evidence, no restore (AC3 — human-thread-only PRs are
+ *                untouched); no clock, no restore. The close proof is
+ *                thread OWNERSHIP, not head position (gh-840 rework
+ *                review, IMPORTANT): a head move with the same open
+ *                machine threads is a silentUpdateBranch refresh, not a
+ *                close — a healthy close resolves the machine threads
+ *                ('no-unresolved-threads'); a bare head advance must never
+ *                suppress the sweep.
+ *
+ * Pure module — no dmtools globals; smAgent feeds it comment payloads and
+ * applies the decisions. GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, JSON-safe
+ * data only).
+ */
+'use strict';
+
+// gh-840 AC1 bound: N ticks. The SM cron ticks every ~5 min; 30 min = 6
+// ticks — the ticket's "≤6 ticks" self-heal bound. Deployment-tunable via
+// the rule's staleMinutes knob (same shape as sweep_stale_validation).
+var DEFAULT_RESTORE_STALE_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;
+
+// The consumption audit marker — one line, JSON payload, invisible in the
+// rendered PR (same protocol family as the gh-807 verdict marker).
+var CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-consume ';
+var RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-restore ';
+var MARKER_SUFFIX = ' -->';
+
+// The only legal consumption paths (the guard vocabulary):
+//   'dispatch'      — consumeLabels fired after an accepted workflow_dispatch
+//   'cross-anchor'  — consumeLabels fired after the gh-715 cross-anchor
+//                     suppression consumed the request
+var CONSUME_PATHS = ['dispatch', 'cross-anchor'];
+
+function isLegalConsumePath(path) {
+    return CONSUME_PATHS.indexOf(path) !== -1;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the consumption-audit comment body. path must be one of
+ * CONSUME_PATHS; headSha anchors the consumption to the head it was
+ * supposed to rework (the sweep's close-proof check compares the recorded
+ * head against the live head). Returns null on an unbuildable record —
+ * callers skip the post; an unattributed consumption must never exist.
+ */
+function buildConsumeAuditComment(path, headSha, atIso) {
+    if (!isLegalConsumePath(path)) return null;
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        path: path,
+        head: headSha,
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return CONSUME_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🏷️ agent:rework consumed (path: ' + path + ', head ' +
+        String(headSha).substring(0, 7) + ') — gh-840 consumption audit. ' +
+        'The label must come off ONLY via a successful rework close; if no close ' +
+        'follows, the tick sweep re-arms it.';
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the sweep's restore bookkeeping marker (gh-821-style durability:
+ * the next ticks read it as the newest quiet-window anchor, so a restore
+ * whose arm is re-consumed without work re-enters the same bounded cycle
+ * instead of being mistaken for fresh state).
+ */
+function buildRestoreMarkerComment(headSha, reason, atIso) {
+    if (!headSha || typeof headSha !== 'string') return null;
+    var payload = {
+        head: headSha,
+        reason: reason || 'restore',
+        at: atIso || new Date().toISOString()
+    };
+    return RESTORE_MARKER_PREFIX + JSON.stringify(payload) + MARKER_SUFFIX + '\n' +
+        '🔄 rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved (gh-840).';
+}
+
+function extractMarker(body, prefix) {
+    var text = String(body || '');
+    var start = text.indexOf(prefix);
+    if (start === -1) return null;
+    start += prefix.length;
+    var end = text.indexOf(MARKER_SUFFIX, start);
+    if (end === -1) return null;
+    var raw = text.substring(start, end).trim();
+    var parsed;
+    try { parsed = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return null; }

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 841
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/841
- **Title**: gh-840 [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-840` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1084
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T13:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:17:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 4

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The fail-closed design (pure module, machine-gated markers, forge-resistant parsing, comprehensive RED→GREEN tests, hoisted require per gh-823) is solid and both suites pass locally (16/16 unit, 481/481 smAgent). However, the whole mechanism reads the PR head from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which the query layer leaves `null` for both affected rules — so in production no consumption marker is ever stamped and the sweep's latch/in-flight/head-advanced gates are dead code (see blocking comment). One important design gap: any head move (including a silent branch refresh) counts as a "rework close", letting the exact hang this PR fixes slip past the sweep.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `js/smAgent.js:4119` — head sourced from `ticket.pr.headSha` is always `null` for PR-carrier rules (`queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`); audit markers are silently never posted, the sweep never has evidence, and its head-dependent gates no-op. Fix via the existing `prHeadAndLabels` probe + a live-shape (`pr: null`) test.
- ⚠️ `js/smAgent.js:4203` — `headAdvanced` treats any head move as a close proof; a silent refresh after a bogus consumption suppresses the sweep forever with machine threads still open.
- 💡 `js/smAgent.js:4096` — `pullRequestId: prNumber` not stringified (siblings all use `String(prNumber)`).

**Next Steps**:
1. Probe the head via `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` (fallback) in `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`; warn when a consumption can't be attributed.
2. Add tests with the live item shape (`pr: null`) — current fixtures inject `pr.headSha`, masking the defect.
3. Corroborate `head-advanced` (e.g. a concluded leg run on the current head) or restore when machine threads remain open on the advanced head.
4. Follow-up ticket: `arm_rework` (rework-unresolved-threads) shares the same null-`item.pr` assumption, so the gh-806 latch is inert on the PR-carrier arming path too.
